title: gaze, voice-level, timed quiet, no reflex narration

targets.text: Nova now performs asked-for gaze actions (look toward sound, look toward face, lock on a face until released, release), raises or lowers its voice on request, can stay quiet for a set number of minutes and resume on its own, and no longer narrates its own reflexes unless asked — and the cold-boot Kiro degraded-start path has been exercised live
Every item in the announcement is demonstrable on the robot (not only in unit tests) and each maps to at least one confirmed requirement on this frame

Today every body reflex reaching the mind is voiced back: config/nervous-system/rules.yaml:236-242 renders the generic rule/fire template "Your body just reacted on its own — the '{rule}' reflex fired." and the harness system prompt (reachy_nova/harness/app.py:52-64) tells Sonic to 'mention what you did in a few words' with no instruction against describing mechanism
The pre-change journal from 2026-08-26 (or a fresh pat on the unpatched build) shows the 'reflex fired' inject text — the before-state is evidenced, not remembered

Reflex injects become quiet context, not prompts: rewrite rules.yaml inject templates for rule/fire, rule/fire:pat-acknowledge, rule/fire:nova-face-noticed and pat/* as parenthetical situational awareness with no 'reflex'/'rule'/'reacted on its own' wording, and add a system-prompt line in HARNESS_SYSTEM_PROMPT that Nova reacts naturally to body cues and never describes its own mechanism unless asked

After the change, grep of every rendered inject for the pat, face-noticed and generic rule/fire entries contains none of: 'reflex', 'rule', 'reacted on its own', 'leaning', 'antenna' — pinned by a test over rules.yaml rendering

Per-rule voice policy in rules.yaml (a 'voice: silent|brief|free' field, or reuse of urgency) with body reflexes defaulting to silent/brief; rendered into the inject text as an explicit marker Sonic can obey; pinned by tests on rules.yaml rendering
load_rules/rule_for accept a 'voice' field with default 'free'; a test asserts generic rule/fire is 'silent' and that a silent rule still produces an inject (never dropped) carrying the marker

One inject per sense class per cooldown: a sense-class dedupe in NovaBus between route_event and _on_inject (bus.py:574-593) so pat-acknowledge, nova-pat-cheer and any future pat/* topic collapse into one inject within the window
A test feeds two rule/fire events (pat-acknowledge then nova-pat-cheer) within the cooldown window and asserts exactly one inject reaches Sonic; a pat after the window produces a fresh inject

'Why did you do that?' is answerable: keep a small recent-sense ring buffer (last N routed injects with timestamps) next to NovaBus._on_inject or CognitionFeed and expose it to Sonic on request (an inject or a tool), so the answer references the actual last sense event
A test injects three routed senses then asks for recent history and gets them in order with timestamps; the live answer to 'why did you move?' names the actual last sense

The harness gains no motion code for any gaze action: look-toward-sound, look-toward-face and face-lock/release are runtime-side (reachy-mini-cli) behaviors/intents, requested from the harness through the intents spool; the AST boundary test (no reachy_mini import, no set_target) stays green
tests/test_harness_boundary.py stays green after all gaze work: no reachy_mini import and no set_target reference anywhere under reachy_nova/harness/

Refuse look-toward-sound with a named reason when no recent DoA exists: DoaPoller must expose the age of its last good reading (Sense carries no timestamp by design), and the behavior refuses above a staleness threshold (candidate: orient.py's latch_after_s=8 s)

With no DoA reading (or one older than the staleness threshold) run_behavior look-toward-sound returns {ok:false, error:<named reason>} and no head motion; with a fresh reading the head turns within the behavior's yaw clamp

Face position reaches the behavior layer: plumb FaceDetection.bbox_norm (and a last-seen time) from vision/face.py through FaceSenseDriver._detect_once into Sense, since Sense.face is a name string only — look-toward-face and face-lock cannot aim without it
Sense (or a face provider) exposes bbox_norm and last-seen age for the most recent detection, pinned by a test in reachy-mini-cli; look-toward-face refuses with a named reason when no face is known
The face store (embeddings, TTL/enroll tiers) is unchanged: gaze actions read position from the live detection path, not from FaceStore
git diff of the gaze PRs touches nothing under reachy/vision/face_store.py and no FaceStore test changes

Face-lost-while-locked and lock-released are emitted as runtime events and must be registered in reachy/export/runtime.py's raw-action tables (an unknown action is dropped from both stdout and MQTT feeds with REASON_UNKNOWN_EVENT); the harness rules.yaml gains matching entries so they render as quiet context
The new intent actions appear in reachy/export/runtime.py's tables, a test asserts they reach both stdout and MQTT feeds, and rules.yaml has an entry for each so test_rules_coverage stays green

Face-lock is safe to hold indefinitely: it clamps head yaw/pitch like orient-to-sound's max_yaw and never drives the raw compose path unbounded; the goto envelope (goto_intent.py limits) is the reference but is not re-implemented in the harness

A test drives the lock behavior with a face bbox at the frame edge for many ticks and asserts commanded yaw/pitch never exceed the behavior's clamp; a 30-minute live hold shows no motor-temperature or jitter warning in the runtime journal

raise_voice/lower_voice (or set_voice_level) are harness tools over the daemon's GET /api/volume/current and POST /api/volume/set, clamped to [10,100], reusing speaking.py's _post + NOVA_DAEMON_URL lifted into a shared daemon-client helper; results follow the {ok:true,volume} / {ok:false,error} contract; EXPECTED_TOOLS in tests/test_harness_tools.py updated

With a stubbed daemon client: raise from 95 clamps to 100 with a named result, lower from 15 clamps to 10, each call returns {ok:true, volume:N}; a daemon HTTP failure returns {ok:false, error}; EXPECTED_TOOLS updated
No runtime-side (reachy-mini-cli) change for volume: the runtime has zero volume surface and the harness already speaks to the daemon over HTTP
git diff of the volume PR touches only reachy_nova/ (no reachy-mini-cli change); the runtime's tests are untouched

The quiet gate lives in one place — SonicSpeaker (speaking.py _enqueue/_play_one) — as a monotonic deadline behind the existing lock/epoch pattern; while armed, utterances are dropped at the playback boundary and hearing/transcription continue untouched
With the deadline armed, a test enqueues an utterance and asserts poster is never called while hearing.feed keeps being invoked; after the deadline passes the next utterance plays

Quiet deadline (and last volume level) persist across harness restarts as small JSON files under the state dir written with the atomic tmp+os.replace pattern (precedent: network_change_path); the deadline is shown in supervisor.status() and logged as one latched [SENSE stage=supervise ... event=quiet] until=<ts> line

A restart of the harness with a future quiet deadline on disk comes up still silent and status() shows quiet_until; a persisted volume level is re-applied on start only if the daemon reports a different value
The harness has no HTTP /api of its own — reachy_nova/api_routes.py belongs to the legacy main.py dashboard — so 'visible in /api status' (#19) means supervisor.status() JSON, not a new HTTP server
No new HTTP server or FastAPI route is added under reachy_nova/harness/; quiet_until and volume appear in supervisor.status() JSON and in the journal

The degraded-start path is exercised on the robot without a reboot: a chaos case 5 in tests/chaos/ON_ROBOT.md sets KIRO_CLI_BIN to a non-existent path, restarts reachy-nova-harness with FORGE_WRITER=kiro, asserts 'started degraded (initial spawn failed' and 'started name=kiro_session' with no 'start failed', then restores the binary and asserts 'recovered' with no manual restart
tests/chaos/ON_ROBOT.md gains case 5 and its journal evidence (started degraded → recovered, no 'start failed', NRestarts unchanged) is recorded in the delivery record, upgrading h12 from low

Radio-off + harness restart is NOT a reproduction (Kiro spawned offline in 14 s on 2026-08-26); the boot-ordering race itself (network-online.target reached before wlan0 associates) is only provable by a deliberate power-cycle with the AP unavailable

The delivery record states the radio-off attempt as non-reproducing and cites the KIRO_CLI_BIN drill as the evidence for the degraded-start path, without claiming the boot-ordering race was reproduced

Ori as the person in the room with the robot (petting it, asking it to look, to speak up, to be quiet), the reachy_nova harness maintainers, and the reachy-mini-cli runtime that gains the gaze behaviors
The exported spec names these three audiences and every requirement is traceable to at least one of them

The robot can be asked to look at a sound or a face, to hold a face until told to let go, to speak louder or softer, and to keep quiet for a set time — and a pat gets one natural reaction, never a description of its own reflex arc; the cold-boot Kiro degraded start has been exercised on the robot by a repeatable drill
Each clause of the after-state maps to a line in the success signal (c33) that was checked live and recorded in the delivery record

Live on 2026-08-26 the robot narrated its own reflexes twice per pat, volume was changed over SSH by hand, and there was no way to ask it to look somewhere or to be quiet — the companion feel breaks when the body's plumbing shows and the only controls are an operator's shell
The delivery record links each of the three 2026-08-26 pain points (narrated reflexes, SSH volume, no gaze/quiet control) to the change that removed it

On the robot: a pat yields at most one short reaction with no sentence containing 'reflex', 'rule' or 'reacted on its own'; 'speak up'/'quieter' move the daemon volume one step with a brief acknowledgement; 'stay silent for 2 minutes' produces zero playbacks for 2 minutes despite pats and questions and resumes without announcement; 'look at me' / 'look at the sound' / 'keep looking at me' / 'you can look away' each produce the motion or a named refusal; chaos case 5 shows 'started degraded' then 'recovered' with no manual restart; uv run pytest green in both repos
Every line of the success signal is executed on the robot and its journal evidence pasted into the delivery record; unit-only claims are labelled as such

lock_face and release_face are exposed as harness tools (tools.py builders + EXPECTED_TOOLS + Sonic tool descriptions) returning the engine's typed result verbatim under the existing {ok:true}/{ok:false,error}/{ok:null,submitted} contract; look-toward-sound and look-toward-face ride the existing run_behavior tool

test_harness_tools.py EXPECTED_TOOLS includes lock_face and release_face; a fake-engine test round-trips each with the typed result; release of an inactive lock returns ok:true with a named no-op reason

stay_silent(minutes, bounded 1-180) and end_silence() are harness tools; entering acknowledges once briefly, asking again while silent extends the deadline (later wins) with a named result, ending early or on expiry is silent by default; nervous-system rules that would speak are rendered with the quiet marker while the deadline is armed

A test asserts: first call acknowledges and arms; second call with a longer duration extends (later wins) and returns a named 'extended' result; end_silence clears; minutes outside 1-180 refuse without arming

A face-lock cannot outlive its mind or its body: the runtime releases the lock (named event) when the harness's retained reachy/state/nova availability goes offline or after a configurable max hold; and because intents are in-memory (a runtime restart drops them), the harness treats an engine-heartbeat loss as 'lock released' with one named line rather than believing it is still locked

Test: engine heartbeat lost while locked -> harness logs lock released reason=engine-restart and the next lock_face succeeds; runtime test: mind offline for the grace period -> lock released event emitted, inhibitions restored

lock_face's inhibition snapshot is not stale-restored: a set_inhibition arriving while locked replaces the snapshot (later wins) and the lock re-adds its own inhibitions on top; release restores the latest snapshot, never the original one
Test: lock (snapshot A) -> set_inhibition B while locked -> release -> inhibitions == B, not A; a second test with no intervening call restores A

A quiet-mode drop is not a playback failure: dropped utterances never arm the echo gate, never purge the queue, and never fire on_playback_failure; each drop logs one latched [SENSE stage=speak event=quiet-drop] line (first drop and count on release, not one per utterance)

Test: with the deadline armed, three utterances enqueued -> poster not called, on_playback_failure not called, gate never armed, exactly one senselog drop line; on release one summary line with count=3

The stay_silent acknowledgement is not eaten by its own gate: the deadline arms only after the acknowledgement utterance that follows the tool result has been played (or after a short grace if none arrives), so 'okay, quiet for ten minutes' is heard and the next utterance is the first one dropped
Test: tool result returned -> next utterance plays and arms the gate -> the utterance after it is dropped; a tool result followed by no utterance within the grace still arms

Sense-class dedupe (c6) is driven by an explicit 'sense: pat|face|sound|vision|...' field on rules.yaml entries (alongside voice); entries without it dedupe by their exact key, and Kiro-authored rules that fall to generic rule/fire dedupe by rule name — the class is never inferred from free-form rule names
Test: rule/fire:pat-acknowledge and rule/fire:nova-pat-cheer both carry sense: pat and collapse; two generic rule/fire events with different rule names within the window both inject

Version skew across the two repos is a named refusal, not a crash: a harness sending lock_face/release_face to an older runtime receives the engine's {ok:false, error:"unknown kind 'lock_face'"} and Sonic says the body did not respond; the delivery record states the required deploy order (runtime first, then harness)
Test: KindRegistry without lock_face returns the unknown-kind refusal for a spooled lock_face command (control.py:321); harness tool test asserts the refusal is passed through verbatim

Every new state is visible and recoverable without SSH: volume changes log one [SENSE stage=act ...] line with old/new levels; the quiet deadline and lock state appear in supervisor.status() (lock read from the runtime's state.json intents view); end_silence and release_face are always accepted even when the harness believes nothing is armed/locked (named no-op), so a confused state is always escapable by voice
Test: status() shows quiet_until and lock fields; end_silence with no deadline returns {ok:true, note:'not silent'}; release_face with no lock returns the runtime's named no-op verbatim
